704071.t: Probably from Proto-Indo-European *(h₁)ey, a locative form of *ís (“this”). See its sense, “that”, in ἐπεί (epeí) and compare the history of Latin sī.

704068.t: PIE word *swé Probably from Ancient Greek ἔθω (éthō, “I am accustomed, wont (to something)”) + -νος (-nos), equivalent to Proto-Indo-European *swedʰ-no-, expanded from the reflexive pronoun Proto-Indo-European *swé (“self”) + *dʰeh₁- (“to put, place, set”).

704098.t: According to Beekes and Chantraine, probably from Pre-Greek. Older theories link the word to εἴρω (eírō, “to fasten together”) or εἴρω (eírō, “to speak, say”); compare ῥήτρα (rhḗtra, “verbal agreement, treaty”).

704093.t: From Proto-Hellenic *ehmi, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁ésmi (“to be, to exist”). Cognate with Old English eom (whence English am), Latin sum, Sanskrit अस्मि॑ (ásmi), Old Armenian եմ (em), and so on.

704069.t: From Proto-Indo-European *swe-dʰh₁- (“custom, character”), from the reflexive pronoun *swé (“self”) + *dʰeh₁- (“to put, place, set”), equivalent to the acc. ἕ (hé) of οὗ (hoû, “him”) + τίθημι (títhēmi, “to set”).

704074.t: From Proto-Hellenic *wéidos, from Proto-Indo-European *wéydos (“seeing, image”), from *weyd- (“to see”). Cognate to Sanskrit वेद॑स् (védas), Proto-Slavic *vidъ, English wit; see also εἴδομαι (eídomai, “to appear, seem, resemble”).

704085.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *dwóh₁ Proto-Indo-European *dwi- Proto-Indo-European *déḱm̥ Proto-Indo-European *(h₁)wídḱm̥ti Proto-Hellenic *ewī́kəti Ancient Greek εἴκοσι From Proto-Hellenic *ewī́kəti, from Proto-Indo-European *(h₁)wídḱm̥ti (“twenty”).

704089.t: Perhaps from a Proto-Indo-European *weyk- (“to resemble”), and cognate with ἔοικα (éoika, “to seem (likely that)”), εἴκελος (eíkelos, “like, similar”), εἰκάζω (eikázō, “to portray, liken”), and others; however, no certain cognates exist outside of Greek.

704036.t: From Proto-Hellenic *hédrā, from Proto-Indo-European *sedreh₂, from *sed- (“to sit”) (whence ἕζομαι (hézomai, “I sit”) and many others).

704013.t: Nominalised neuter form of ἐγχειρίδιος (enkheirídios, “fitting in the hand”) derived from χείρ (kheír, “hand”).

704032.t: From ἔδω (édō, “to eat”) and the suffix -μα (-ma).

704088.t: From Proto-Hellenic *wéikō, from Proto-Indo-European *weyk- (“to curve, bend; exchange”).

704081.t: Possibly from a Proto-Indo-European *weyk- (“to become equal”), although there are no cognates outside of Greek. Cognate with εἰκών (eikṓn), ἔοικα (éoikă).

704022.t: Probably from ἕδος (hédos, “seat”) + a suffix -(α)φος (-(a)phos), though Beekes expresses some doubt, perhaps due to the strange morphology of the suffix.

704091.t: Of uncertain origin. Traditionally derived as a compound of εἵλη (heílē, “heat or warmth of the sun”) + κρίνω (krínō, “to separate, distinguish”) + -ης (-ēs, “adjectival suffix”), thus "distinguished in or by the sun".

704000.t: From rare ἐγκύω (enkŭ́ō, “to be pregnant”) + -ος (-os), from ἐν- (en-, “in-”) + κύω (kŭ́ō, “to conceive”).

704015.t: From ἐν- (en-, “in”) + χρίω (khrī́ō, “to rub, smear; anoint”).

704073.t: From εἴδομαι (eídomai, “to appear, seem”) + -σις (-sis, abstract noun suffix).
